title: Install procedure leaves target/release/termal absent for minutes on DL560 (cargo clean + in-place build); switch to separate target dir + atomic rename
outcome:
Installing a landed TermAl build never makes the installed binary path disappear, so sessions that start or call TERMAL_CLI during an install never see "No such file or directory".

The occurrence: the Engram runner (DL560 session-4) saw /home/greg/github/TermAl/target/release/termal missing at 2026-11-08T00:14:42Z (reported by Engram 12329 #155). Opus2 confirmed the cause (#4965). The DL560 install of ba6c9846 ran `cargo clean --release -p termal` and then rebuilt in the master checkout's own target/, so the path was absent from about 00:14 to about 00:18Z. The fdbb53c8 install used the same procedure.

This is not the product defect in w-f5b824b8e5d6 ("(deleted)"). That fix's /proc/<pid>/exe fallback is why the MCP tools kept working.
acceptance: The integration owner's documented install procedure builds in a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR, never in the master checkout's target/. It stages the new binary beside the installed path, keeps a backup of the old binary, and replaces it on Linux and macOS with an atomic rename over the path, so the path always exists. On Windows it uses rename-aside followed immediately by rename-in from the same volume.
The next install on each host records the times of its rename steps and confirms that the path existed throughout, on Linux, or that the gap was only the rename-aside to rename-in window, on Windows.

completion.summary:
The install procedure is fixed and verified on both hosts. Builds go to a separate target (target/install-target) and never clean or rebuild in place in target/release. The live binary is swapped by staging termal.new, taking a hard-link or copy backup, and then:
- Linux: an atomic `mv -f`;
- Windows: a same-volume rename-aside of the running exe followed at once by the rename-in.
Recorded with project memory termal-install-procedure-atomic. Next-install evidence:
- DL560, fdd8d035: termal.new at 01:25:03.605Z, hard-link backup at 01:25:03.948Z, atomic mv at 01:25:04.635Z. The path was never absent.
- Central, fdd8d035: rename-aside 01:16:45.709Z, rename-in done 01:16:45.832Z. Absent for at most about 0.12 s, versus about 4.5 min under the old procedure on DL560.
No acceptance evaluation exists for this item, as Fable2 directed.
